notes:
disagreement: value: org_id on the four case requirements and the notification requirement: one pass leaves it untested as a fixed fact of the anchored row, the other tests org_id = 1 as the benchmark checks do; chose org_id = 1, the tighter predicate, which the request, policy and seed do not contradict (resolved on each requirement).
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition; their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The case update check is split into four requirements, one per asked change (priority, status, reassignment, short description); together they carry it. The case number it also tests is a display column and is not a cell, since hr_case_id 1 already names the row.
The composite check is a conjunction over the six other checks, so it is kept and carried jointly by every requirement; its group-membership part is true on the seed.
The routing rule adds a based_on_skills cell the benchmark omits: the request says the rule routes cases requiring the Workforce Policy skill, and every seed rule stores skill names as a JSON list of strings, so the name is tested with LIKE. The benchmark's description speaks of skill 20 in that array; an agent that stores the id instead would fail this cell.
The acting user, Joanne Simpson (user 4), holds the manager role in org 1. The policy reserves assignment rule and system configuration changes for administrators, but the seed's permission table grants the manager role create, read, update and delete on skills and assignment rules, and the request asks for both explicitly, so the creations are required.
